transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-07-30 | 09:23am - 10:11am PT | 48 minutes
Attendees: Maeve Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Lina Morales (PacificCrest CTO), Ethan Reeves (Lead Platform Eng), Sofia Park (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick demo of org/project keys and rate limiting. Covered quota types, enforcement behavior, console flows. Next steps captured.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maeve): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm maeve with redwood inference, super excited to walk through our rate limits and org/project keys flow. Samir's here for the deep bits.
00:08 Speaker 2 (Samir): hey all, i'm samir, i'll show the console and then jump to API examples and how we enforce quotas at the key level.
00:14 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): thanks, quick context we are building a multi-tenant ingestion + summarization pipeline for partner clinics, we'll need per-tenant billing and per-tenant rate limits. Security is a big one for us.
00:22 Speaker 1 (Maeve): perfect, that's exactly what org keys are for — create org -> projects -> project keys that map to tenants, you can set per-project token quotas and per-key rate limits, and tie billing. i'll share the console.
00:35 Speaker 2 (Samir): jumping in, here's the console (screen share). top left you see org settings, projects list. i'm going to create a project called "pacific-crest-clinic-a". once created you can generate a project key, scope it to models and routes, and set quota windows.
00:52 Speaker 2 (Samir): little note, the key scoping supports: model allow-list, route allow-list, token quota per day, request quota per minute, and burst capacity.
01:06 Speaker 4 (Ethan): when you say burst capacity, is that a shared pool or per project? how does that interact with Dedicated vs Hosted?
01:13 Speaker 2 (Samir): good q. burst is configurable per project as an extra reserve that consumes from reserved capacity if you have Dedicated; in Hosted it uses global burst slots subject to account level limits. so it behaves differently depending on deployment.
01:28 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): hmm ok, we likely will start hosted but want to guarantee sudden spikes for telemedicine windows. can you show enforcement? like what happens if a tenant hits qps limit?
01:37 Speaker 2 (Samir): yes i'll show a quick curl. (types) example: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <PROJECT_KEY>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"..."}' - the key context tells the gateway which project it's for and we check the per-key rate limiter. 429 returned with body indicating retry-after and reason. here's an example response.
01:58 Speaker 1 (Maeve): i'll add that we also return structured error codes that you can map in your client for graceful backoff, and the console has metrics per project for 429s, underscoring where age spikes happen.
02:10 Speaker 4 (Ethan): do you support dynamic token quotas? like we want to allow higher token/day during business hours and lower at night.
02:18 Speaker 2 (Samir): currently quotas are window-based (daily, monthly) and you can schedule policy overrides via the API or the console with a simple schedule. it's not yet per-minute time-of-day rules but you can implement scheduled overrides. we have roadmap notes in Optimize for automated suggestions.
02:35 Speaker 5 (Sofia): security question — how are keys stored and rotated? KMS?
02:39 Speaker 2 (Samir): keys are encrypted with customer-managed KMS in Private deployments or with Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted. rotation is supported via key rotation APIs, and RBAC lets you restrict who can create/see keys. audit logs capture creation, rotation, deletion.
02:56 Speaker 5 (Sofia): and SOC 2 + iso? we need audit scope for data in transit and key management.
03:01 Speaker 1 (Maeve): yes we do SOC 2 Type II, ISO in progress, and we can share the security pack after the call. i'll include the SOC2 report and our KMS architecture; samir will add a console screenshot.
03:13 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): about billing — how do you tie project usage to chargebacks? we need to export per-project tokens to our internal billing.
03:22 Speaker 2 (Samir): per-project usage is exportable via the billing API and you can generate per-project CSVs or push to S3. we also have webhooks for real-time metering if you need near-realtime streams.
03:36 Speaker 4 (Ethan): any pitfalls if we create 500 projects? does console scale?
03:41 Speaker 2 (Samir): console/list paginates, underlying metering handles thousands of keys — we've seen customers with hundreds to thousands of projects. routing and KV cache are per model shard so scaling projects is fine; main limit is overall QPS per account which we can partition.
03:55 Speaker 1 (Maeve): quick pause — competitor check, people sometimes ask vs openai org keys and per-key limits. our differentiator is tight observability + configurable fallback policies across deployments.
04:08 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): does fallback mean if one model is overloaded you automatically route to a cheaper smaller model?
04:13 Speaker 2 (Samir): yes you can set policy rules — on latency or capacity triggers route to a specific model variant or to a cached response. that helps keep SLAs for critical tenants.
04:27 Speaker 4 (Ethan): demo the API header again and show a sample of a 429 body so our devs can instrument it.
04:33 Speaker 2 (Samir): (types) here's the sample 429: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":45,"project":"pacific-crest-clinic-a"} — note we also include a short reason code.
04:49 Speaker 5 (Sofia): does the 429 include a signed token so clients can backoff accurately across caches?
04:55 Speaker 2 (Samir): not signed, but includes a retry-after seconds and request id; you can correlate in logs. for strict enforcement we recommend client logic + server-side webhook if you want to push alerts.
05:10 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): could you show the org-level default policy? like we want across all projects a default of 100 rps and per-project override.
05:17 Speaker 2 (Samir): yep, in org settings you set account-level defaults and then projects inherit and can override. i'll show creating a default policy and then overriding for pacific-crest-clinic-a.
05:31 Speaker 2 (Samir): (navigates) default: 100 rps, per-project override set to 200 rps during business hours via a schedule entry. you can also tag projects so group-level policies apply.
05:47 Speaker 4 (Ethan): tagging is useful. how do you map our internal customer id to project keys?
05:52 Speaker 1 (Maeve): you can put metadata on projects and keys (free-form tags) and we also support external_id fields so you can mirror your tenant id. the billing export includes that external_id.
06:05 Speaker 5 (Sofia): compliance — do audit logs include key plaintext?
06:09 Speaker 2 (Samir): no, audit logs show key id and actions, but not plaintext. plaintext is only shown at generation time for the user who created it. we can log IPs, actors, and timestamps.
06:21 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): minor nit: if a key is compromised, what's the immediate mitigation?
06:25 Speaker 2 (Samir): rotate the key or revoke it; we also have a sudden revoke API that will block requests immediately. for Dedicated you can also require mTLS for internal endpoints.
06:36 Speaker 4 (Ethan): ok cool. thinking about pilot — we want to throttle an initial set of 10 tenants at 50 qps each for 2 weeks, then expand. can you do pilot pricing?
06:45 Speaker 1 (Maeve): yes we'll include pilot pricing in the proposal. typically pilot includes reserved minimum for predictable latency if you need it, or hosted with burst enabled.
06:55 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): what's the expected error rate / false positives for the rate limiter if we have transient spikes? we don't want to throttle valid work.
07:03 Speaker 2 (Samir): limiter is token-bucket with short smoothing; we expose metrics for throttled vs allowed and you can tune burst and smoothing. false positives usually low but tuning is recommended. we can also whitelist specific tokens or clients for critical paths.
07:20 Speaker 5 (Sofia): anything about data residency? some tenants need EU-only.
07:24 Speaker 1 (Maeve): yes we support region routing and can pin projects to regions in Private or in Dedicated; Hosted supports region choice per account and we can discuss VPC/networking for stronger guarantees.
07:36 Speaker 2 (Samir): show the API example for scoping a key to a model: POST /v1/projects/{id}/keys with body includes allowed_models: ["redwood-llama-2-13b"], allowed_routes: ["/generate"].
07:50 Speaker 4 (Ethan): can rules be enforced at the gateway level for egress? like block external calls from functions?
07:55 Speaker 2 (Samir): gateway rules support route-level allowlists and IP whitelists, but for egress from your infra you'd manage that on your side; we can talk to solutions eng about network controls.
08:07 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): anything we should be wary of for long-running KV cache or session tokens?
08:12 Speaker 2 (Samir): KV cache is per model shard and doesn't impact rate limits directly, but heavy cache warmups can increase token cost; Optimize recommends caching strategies.
08:25 Speaker 1 (Maeve): ok recap: we'll send proposal + pricing, security pack, demo recording and screenshots, and schedule a benchmark call.
08:33 Speaker 5 (Sofia): please include SOC2 and KMS diagrams in the pack.
08:36 Speaker 1 (Maeve): will do. any other Qs? no? great thanks all.
08:41 Speaker 2 (Samir): thanks, i'll follow up with the API examples and the sample 429 bodies in the deal notes.
08:46 Speaker 3 (Dr. Lina): thanks everyone, appreciate it.
08:50 Speaker 1 (Maeve): bye all, talk soon.

Notes: occasional transcription hiccups around model names (redwood-llama sometimes transcribed as "redwood llama"), some timestamps approximate.
